name: North Carolina free accredited veterans claims assistance
organization: North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
description: State and county service officers help veterans and qualifying survivors with benefits claims.
next_step: Choose your county veterans contact or the assigned state service center. Ask for an accredited representative, an appointment and the records needed for your claim. Use the statewide number for routing.
constraints: State services are free; a referral does not establish benefit eligibility.
The statewide number is a department routing line, not a direct claims appointment line.

name: North Carolina state veterans homes
organization: North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
description: Published state veterans home information and admissions contacts.
next_step: Open the state homes directory and choose the home. Ask its admissions team about eligibility, assessment, payer arrangements and current intake.
constraints: The statewide department phone is a routing fallback, not an admissions line.
The Fayetteville State Veterans Home page states the facility is closed for replacement; do not use it as an available placement.
Confirm current operating status and admission availability for the particular home.

name: North Carolina aging information and options counseling
description: Local information and options counseling helps older adults choose community and long-term support.
next_step: Use your county-matched aging agency or the linked Information and Assistance Provider Directory. Explain the person’s needs and ask which local provider offers options counseling.
constraints: The published service is for people age 60 or older and those acting on their behalf.
No dedicated statewide options-counseling phone is published on the reviewed page; the county aging contact is the starting route.
For all-age disability assistance, use NCATP, Independent Living information or NC 211 as appropriate.

name: North Carolina Area Agencies on Aging directory
description: Official county map identifies 16 regional aging agencies.
next_step: Choose your county in the map or this guide to call the matched agency. If you cannot identify the region, ask the NCDHHS Customer Service Center for aging-service routing.
constraints: 800-662-7030 is the NCDHHS Customer Service Center, not a dedicated aging or eligibility line.

name: North Carolina SHIIP Medicare counseling
description: Free, unbiased counseling on Medicare coverage, prescription plans and related insurance questions.
next_step: Call SHIIP and request a local counselor. Ask about your coverage question and any help with Medicare costs.
constraints: Counseling does not itself enroll someone in a plan or establish eligibility for financial assistance.

name: North Carolina CAP/DA Medicaid home and community services
description: CAP/DA supports qualifying disabled adults who need an institutional level of care to remain in or return to the community.
next_step: Open the CAP/DA page and its NC LIFTSS link to find a case management entity serving the applicant’s county. Ask for a referral and assessment. NC LIFTSS can help route questions at 833-522-5429. Ask about project exclusions: CAP/DA does not cover modifications during new construction or nonportable modifications to a rented residence.
constraints: Adults must meet disability, care-need and long-term-care Medicaid rules and be enrolled in NC Medicaid Direct; Medicaid enrollment alone does not establish CAP/DA eligibility.
Ask the case manager about the needs assessment, service plan, required documentation, authorization and accepted providers before ordering equipment or arranging work.
Policy 3K-2 excludes modification during new construction and nonportable modifications in rented residences. A referral does not guarantee a waiver slot, approval or funding.

name: North Carolina statewide long-term-care ombudsman
description: State and 16 regional offices help residents address rights and care concerns in long-term-care facilities.
next_step: Use the county-matched regional contact first. Give the facility location and resident’s wishes; if the region is unclear, ask the state office for ombudsman routing.
constraints: The state number is the office line published in the regional directory; ask for the long-term-care ombudsman program.
Not an emergency response line or a guarantee of a particular outcome.

name: North Carolina Family Caregiver Support Program
description: Local caregiver support can include information, training, counseling, short-term respite and limited supplemental services.
next_step: Call your county aging agency and ask for the Family Caregiver Support Program. Describe the care recipient’s age and needs and ask about respite and caregiver training.
constraints: This program does not pay family members to provide continuous care.
Age, caregiver relationship and program rules apply; services vary locally.
No dedicated statewide public intake phone appears on the reviewed program page.

name: North Carolina Assistive Technology Program
organization: NCDHHS Employment and Independence for People with Disabilities
description: Device demonstrations, short-term loans and reuse help people explore assistive technology.
next_step: Call NCATP or open its Staff and Centers link. Describe the task or barrier and ask for an appropriate center, a demonstration, a device loan or reuse options.
constraints: Ask about stock, assessment needs, fees and suitability.
Device assistance does not promise construction funding or permanent installation.

name: Disability Rights North Carolina
description: North Carolina’s designated protection and advocacy organization provides disability-rights resources and intake.
next_step: Review the resources and Apply for Legal Help instructions or call to ask how to request assistance with a disability-related rights concern.
constraints: The toll-free number is published for calls within North Carolina.
Intake does not guarantee legal representation or a particular result.

name: North Carolina Services for the Blind
organization: NCDHHS Division of Services for the Blind
description: Vision rehabilitation, independent living services and medical eye-care information.
next_step: Ask the division for the district office or social worker serving your county and describe the daily tasks affected by vision loss.
constraints: Ask which program applies and about assessment, eligibility and current availability.

name: North Carolina deaf and hard-of-hearing services
organization: NCDHHS Division of Services for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
description: Regional communication-access services and information on assistive and telecommunications resources.
next_step: Call the published voice number or use the Regional Centers link. Ask about communication technology, accommodations and services appropriate for hearing or combined hearing and vision loss.
constraints: 800-851-6099 is a voice information line, not a relay operator.
The page also publishes TTY 919-715-0933 and videophone 919-890-0859; use the communication route that fits your needs.

name: NC 211 community resource navigation
description: Information and referrals for local health and human services.
next_step: Dial 211 or 888-892-1162 and give your county and immediate practical need. Ask for local housing, food, utility or other service intake contacts.
constraints: A referral does not establish eligibility or confirm openings, housing placement or available funds.

name: North Carolina Independent Living information and intake — purchase pause
organization: NCDHHS Employment and Independence for People with Disabilities
description: Independent Living can assess goals and connect people with supports; new purchased services are currently paused.
next_step: Ask the IL office serving your area about eligibility assessment, the waiting list and alternative funding or services. Existing clients should ask which services are already authorized in their plan.
constraints: As reviewed October 20, 2026, all four priority categories are closed and new or additional purchased IL services have been paused since August 1, 2026.
Applications may still be processed; eligible new applicants are assigned a priority category and waiting list.
Home modifications are a listed IL service, but this entry is not an offer of currently available ramp or bathroom funding.
